questions.prompt: Why must authentication middleware strip `Authorization` headers and password fields before emitting error logs?

options.text: Logging credentials plaintext turns log aggregation tools into exposed breach targets if internal log viewers lack strict access limits
JSON serializers reject string passwords
HttpOnly cookies fail if strings print to console
Passwords exceed stdout buffer limits

questions.explanation: Secret redaction guarantees sensitive tokens never accumulate silently in monitoring backends.

options.text: Path Traversal / Local File Inclusion attempt
Cross-Site Request Forgery
ARP Spoofing
DNS Amplification

questions.explanation: Relative parent sequences (`../`) attempt to break out of the intended folder root.

questions.prompt: Why should logs stream immediately off host servers into append-only central storage?

options.text: To preserve tamper-evident forensics even if a local host is compromised and local `/var/log` is altered
To shrink PostgreSQL CPU load directly
Because local disks refuse plaintext writes
To speed up CSS rendering in browsers

questions.explanation: Remote immutable shipping denies attackers the ability to scrub traces cleanly post-intrusion.

questions.prompt: If an engineer accidentally pushes an active Stripe secret key to a public GitHub repo, simply running a second commit to delete the file is insufficient. Why?

options.text: The secret stays preserved permanently in Git commit history and automated scraper bots harvest pushed keys within seconds—it MUST be revoked/rotated upstream immediately
Git deletes commits only on Linux hosts
Stripe refuses deleting files named `.env`
TLS certificates freeze if files are removed

questions.explanation: Once exposed publicly, treat secrets as burned immediately and revoke/rotate upstream.

questions.prompt: During an active server compromise, why isolate the instance firewall/network BEFORE rebooting or wiping disk?

options.text: Quarantining halts lateral attacker traffic immediately while preserving running process state and forensic evidence for root-cause analysis
Rebooting improves malware scan speeds silently
Firewalls cannot change rules on live servers
Backups overwrite volatile RAM logs automatically

questions.explanation: Stopping network communication preserves forensic artifacts needed to learn how entry occurred.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a 'blameless' post-incident security retrospective?

options.text: Focuses on fixing systemic missing guardrails, tooling alerts, and automated tests rather than punishing individuals who surface issues
Hides breaches permanently from leadership
Skips remediation tickets entirely
Terminates junior developers automatically

questions.explanation: Blameless culture encourages transparent reporting and lasting technical safeguards.
